identity.name: Venetian Modon and Coron
alt_names: The Two Eyes of the Republic

land.text: Modon (Methoni) and Coron (Koroni), the two Venetian fortress towns on the southwest Messenian coast; the pages give no extent for their territory, so the radii are upper bounds

predecessors.note: Koroni was taken 'from Champlitte's men' (Koroni page); Methoni 'along with Koroni' (Methoni page). The Treaty of Sapienza (June 1209) had Geoffrey of Villehardouin recognise the Venetian possession of both.

successors.note: Modon fell on 9 August 1500 after 28 days; Koroni and Navarino on 15 or 17 August 1500. Venice returned in 1686 (Morean War) and lost the peninsula again in 1715; that second period is not drawn here.

capitals.name: Coron (Koroni)
capitals.note: Page silent on a seat of the colony; the Koroni page says the garrison's original two captains resided in Koroni (late 13th century) and that Venetian statutes governed the fortresses from the mid-14th century. Modon (21.70, 36.82) is the other fortress.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Principality of Achaea shape covers the Peloponnese from 1206). Two fortress towns: 'In 1206 or 1207 a Venetian fleet took Koroni'; the Methoni page has Methoni captured 'along with Koroni'. The Methoni page is silent on the extent of the colony, which was a coastal strip around each fortress; 'most of the peninsula was assigned to Venice in the Partitio Romaniae treaty' on paper only.

New keyframe: Navarino added. 'As Achaea weakened, Venetia expanded in Messenia, taking Navarino in 1417.' The page gives no other territorial change. (Reviewer eu-05-x, 2026-10-19: 'to' 1499 -> 1500: Methoni fell 'on 9 August 1500' (Methoni page) and Koroni and Navarino surrendered '15 or 17 August 1500' (Koroni page), so the shape is drawn in 1500, the dissolve year)

region.text: Modon (Methoni) and Coron (Koroni), the two Venetian fortress towns on the southwest Messenian coast; the pages give no extent for their territory, so the radii are upper bounds

ledger.note: 1206 or 1207: Venice takes Modon and Coron. 'A Venetian fleet under Premarini and a son of Doge Enrico Dandolo took Koroni from Champlitte's men'; the Methoni page: 'In 1206 or 1207, a Venetian fleet captured Methoni along with Koroni.' The year is the pages' alternative; 1206 is used. In June 1209 the Treaty of Sapienza had Geoffrey of Villehardouin recognise Venice's possession of both fortresses.

1417: Venice takes Navarino. 'As Achaea weakened, Venetia expanded in Messenia, taking Navarino in 1417.' The page does not name the previous holder; the Principality of Achaea is the researcher's reading.

9 August 1500: Modon falls. 'After 28 days, on 9 August 1500, Methoni fell'; Sultan Bayezid II 'came in person to supervise the siege'. The war page dates the Battle of Modon to August 1500 and has Kemal Reis bombard the fortress from the sea.
15 or 17 August 1500: Coron and Navarino surrender. 'Koroni and Navarino surrendered (15 or 17 August 1500)' in the Second Ottoman-Venetian War.

August 1500: Venetian Modon and Coron end. The war page calls them 'the two eyes of the Republic'; Venice recognised the Ottoman gains in 1503 (Coron, Modon, Durazzo and Lepanto annexed to the Ottomans, Cephalonia and Ithaca to Venice).

wars.name: Venetian seizure of Koroni and Methoni

zones.text: Modon (Methoni) and Coron (Koroni), the two Venetian fortress towns on the southwest Messenian coast; the pages give no extent for their territory, so the radii are upper bounds

wars.outcome: A Venetian fleet took Koroni from Champlitte's men in 1206 or 1207 and Methoni with it; the Treaty of Sapienza (June 1209) had Geoffrey of Villehardouin recognise Venetian possession.
wars.note: Venice had attacked pirates at Methoni in 1125 and had 'its eye on Methoni since the 12th century' (Methoni page).

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian War of 1499-1503
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took Modon in August 1500 (Bayezid II present) and Koroni and Navarino days later; the war ended in 1503 with Venice recognising the Ottoman gains.
wars.note: Lepanto was retaken by Kemal Reis in April-May 1500 after a Venetian attack of December 1499.

certainty.note: The fleet's conquest of 1206 or 1207 and the Achaean frontier before the treaty are undated.
The Treaty of Sapienza (June 1209) recognised the possession of the two fortresses; their hinterland is not described on any page, so only the fortress points are sharp.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row (the Peloponnese is Achaea's); slug free (the Achaea dossier already uses 10 km circles for 'Modon and Coron'). Three pages opened; no single Wikipedia article covers the colony (wikipedia null; the Methoni and Koroni articles are the nearest). Not settled: (1) the extent of the colony's territory (page silent); (2) the previous holder of Navarino in 1417; (3) the second Venetian period 1686-1715 (Morean War, Kingdom of the Morea) is not drawn; (4) the Venetian Argos and Nauplia (1388-1540) and the Venetian Negroponte (1390-1470) are other Venetian possessions for eu-13 or a gap-filler; (5) type colony of the Republic of Venice, family italy; Lepanto is not drawn.
